blocks.caption: A complete controlled form with validation and a busy state.

blocks.text: Things worth copying from that example

items: `htmlFor` on every label, matching the input's `id`. This is what screen readers rely on.
`role="alert"` on error messages so they are announced when they appear.
`disabled` while submitting, to prevent double submissions.
A `finally` block, so a failed request does not leave the button stuck.

blocks.text: For large forms, a library such as React Hook Form removes most of this boilerplate and avoids re-rendering on every keystroke. Learn the manual version first - the library makes far more sense afterwards.

previous.title: Controlled Inputs
previous.description: Binding form fields to state so React is the single source of truth.

blocks.text: A **controlled** input takes its value from state and reports changes back through `onChange`. React holds the truth and the DOM just displays it.
Because the value lives in state, you can validate it, transform it, or reset it from anywhere.
Passing `value` without `onChange` gives you a read-only field and a console warning. Add the handler, or use `defaultValue` if you genuinely want an uncontrolled input.
One state object for a whole form
Rather than a `useState` per field, many forms keep one object and a shared change handler. The `name` attribute picks the field to update.
Never initialise a controlled input to `undefined` or `null`. React starts it as uncontrolled and warns loudly when a value appears later. Use an empty string.
